stages.change: Used a continuing cover, unboxed section heading and natural query flow. The source tables still crossed a page boundary.
Set the existing Cyrillic title as a single Calibri line, used Cambria for section heads, and combined the two source tables on page 1.

findings.evidence: The isolated cover leaves the first example on page 2. An explicit break separates the diagram from the query.
findings.correction: Let the illustration and first content section share page flow; drop the forced query break.
findings.result: The illustration and the first source table are in the opening sequence, and the diagram leads directly into the query on page 2.

findings.evidence: The baseline CLI asks for Literata and resolves to Georgia on this host.
findings.correction: Select a locally verified family for each type role and inspect the actual diagnostic text runs.
findings.result: The final renderer uses Calibri Bold display, Cambria Bold section headings and Consolas SQL.

findings.evidence: The first trial puts authors on page 1 and books on page 2. Readers must turn the page to compare the keys.
findings.correction: Use a one-line display title and tighter cover transition while keeping 12 pt body text and two complete source tables.
findings.result: Both source tables are together on page 1. The diagram, query, result and exercise stay together on page 2.

findings.evidence: The Word Accessibility Assistant opened and requested format conversion before offering checker results. Word reports Compatibility Mode for the generated DOCX.
findings.correction: Evaluate an explicit modern Word compatibility target with an independent package, layout and accessibility regression.
